Numbers k > 2 such that the Diophantine equation x^2 + 2^a * 5^b * 13^c = y^k has one or more solutions for nonnegative a, b, c with x, y > 0 and gcd(x, y) = 1.
Numbers with primitive English number names.
Numbers k such that the product of their digits divides both k and R(k), where R(k) is the digits reverse of k.
A self-describing sequence: the zeros and ones in the decimal representation of the sequence correspond to the binary representation of the sequence.
Irregular table: row n (n >= 0) is obtained by listing numbers 0 .. A018819(n)-1.
Relative of Hofstadter Q-sequence: a(n) = n for 1 <= n <= 8; a(n) = a(n-a(n-1)) + a(n-a(n-2)) for n > 8.
Relative of Hofstadter Q-sequence: a(n) = n for 1 <= n <= 9; a(n) = a(n-a(n-1)) + a(n-a(n-2)) for n > 9.
Relative of Hofstadter Q-sequence: a(n) = n for 1 <= n <= 10; a(n) = a(n-a(n-1)) + a(n-a(n-2)) for n > 10.
Relative of Hofstadter Q-sequence: a(n) = n for 1 <= n <= 11; a(n) = a(n-a(n-1)) + a(n-a(n-2)) for n > 11.
Relative of Hofstadter Q-sequence: a(n) = n for 1 <= n <= 12; a(n) = a(n-a(n-1)) + a(n-a(n-2)) for n > 12.
Relative of Hofstadter Q-sequence: a(n) = n for 1 <= n <= 13; a(n) = a(n-a(n-1)) + a(n-a(n-2)) for n > 13.
Irregular triangle read by rows: row n (n >= 0) is obtained by listing numbers 0 .. A000123(n)-1.
Numbers n such that abs(n - rev(n)) is a square, where rev(n) is the decimal reverse of n (A004086).
Numbers n such that the Shimura subgroup Sigma(n) of the Jacobi variety J_0(n) has order 1.
A prime mountain: peaks and valleys beyond the origin correspond to prime abscissa (see Comments for precise definition).
Hexagonal spiral constructed on the nodes of the triangular net in which each new term is the sum of its two largest neighbors in the structure.
Rook's moves in chess: possible difference between origin and destination square when the squares are numbered sequentially, row by row.
Queen's moves in chess: possible difference between origin and destination square when the squares are numbered sequentially, row by row.
Between two successive digits "8" there are 0, then 1, then 2, then 3, ... other digits.
Between two successive digits "9" there are 0, then 1, then 2, then 3, ... other digits.
Between two successive digits "0" there are 0, then 1, then 2, then 3, ... other digits.
Triangle read by rows: row n consists of k, 1<=k<=n, such that binomial(n,k) is divisible by gcd(n,k).
Maximum starting value of X such that repeated replacement of X with X-ceiling(X/9) requires n steps to reach 0.
Maximum starting value of X such that repeated replacement of X with X-ceiling(X/10) requires n steps to reach 0.
Numbers n for which the number of distinct prime divisors of binomial(n,k) has a "local maximum" (see the unusual meaning given in comment) at k = floor(n/2).
Rows of the self-orthogonal Latin squares of order 8, lexicographically sorted.
Irregular triangle read by rows: possible numbers of diagonals of an n-edged convex polyhedron.
Irregular triangle read by rows: possible numbers of diagonals of convex polyhedra having n vertices.
a(n) = smallest k with digit product A002473(n).
Numbers that are divisible by the sum of their digits and for which the sum of digits equals the product of digits.
The palindromic kernel of n in base 2 (with carryless GF(2)[X] factorization): a(n) = A091255(n,A057889(n)).
Natural numbers whose digits can be formed by typing adjacent keys on a 123-456-789 keypad without repeating a digit.

Numbers ending with their digital root in decimal representation.

Numbers m>0 such that m = k*(reversal of k*m) for some k<=m.
Numbers k with the property that (sum of digits of k) times (number of digits of k) equals (sum of {each digit of k} raised to the power {number of digits in k}).
Numbers k with the property that the square root of the product of the digits of k is equal to the sum of the square roots of its digits.
a(n+1) is the smallest number greater than a(n) such that Sum_{j=1..n+1} 1/a(j) <= 4, a(1) = 1.
Nonnegative numbers whose digits can be formed by typing adjacent keys on a 123-456-789-0XX keypad without repeating a digit.
Nonnegative numbers whose digits can be formed by typing adjacent keys on a 789-456-123-00X keypad without repeating a digit.
Numbers that are equal to a product of powers of digits where the exponents from left to right decrease with 1 and the exponent for the units digit is 1.
Natural numbers whose digits can be formed by typing non-adjacent keys on a 123-456-789 keypad without repeating a digit.

Numbers that are not the sum of abundant numbers (not necessarily distinct).
Numbers m such that 2^m + 1 has at most 2 distinct prime factors.
Numbers of variables for which the Shapiro inequality holds.

Interspersion of the signature sequence of sqrt(1/2).

Numbers whose sum of digits are congruent (mod 10) to the string 1,2, ..., 9.

Corresponding values of geometric means of digits of numbers from A061430.
Numbers k for which A065642(k) = A285109(k).
Numbers k such that the k-th term of some (generalized) Lucas sequence has no primitive prime factor.

Numbers k such that k^2 + 1 is 100-smooth.
Lexicographically earliest sequence of distinct positive terms such that, for any n>0, n and a(n) differ and overlap in base 10 (in the sense of A262323).
Numbers n for which A000010(n) = A285699(n); positions of zeros in A285709.

a(n) = a(n - a(n - 2)) + a(n - a(n - 8)), with a(i) = i for 1 <= i <= 9.

A slow relative of Hofstadter's Q sequence.
(Product of distinct prime factors)^(Product of prime exponents).
Numbers having at most one odd prime factor to an odd power in their prime factorization.
Numbers k such that, for any divisor d of k, the digital sum of d divides k.
Numbers n such that, for any i and j with i >= j >= 0, ds^i(n) divides ds^j(n) (where ds^k denotes the k-th iteration of the digital sum).
a(n) is the number of zeros of the Chebyshev S(n, x) polynomial (A049310) in the open interval (-sqrt(3), +sqrt(3)).
Self-inverse permutation: in base 3, reverse the lengths of runs of consecutive equal digits.

Restricted growth sequence computed for sigma, A000203.
Maximum number of binary vectors of length n such that the union (or bitwise OR) of any 2 distinct vectors does not contain any other vector.
Numbers k, not ending in 0, such that inserting a 0 between each pair of adjacent digits results in a multiple of k.
Positive numbers m with the property that m is the least cyclic permutation of its digits with the same number of digits as m.
Numbers whose cyclic permutations are pairwise coprime.
Positions of 0 in A287457; complement of A287186.
Seven steps forward, six steps back.
Eight steps forward, seven steps back.
Nine steps forward, eight steps back.
Ten steps forward, nine steps back.
Start with n and repeatedly apply the powertrain map x -> A133500(x); a(n) is the fixed point that is eventually reached, or -1 if the trajectory never reaches a fixed point.

Lexicographically earliest sequence of distinct positive terms such that, if digsum(a(i)) = digsum(a(j)), then either i = j or digsum(a(i+1)) != digsum(a(j+1)) (where digsum is the digital sum, A007953).
Lexicographically earliest sequence of distinct positive terms such that, for any i and j > 0, a(i*j) != a(i) * a(j).
Lexicographically earliest sequence of distinct positive terms such that the sum of two consecutive terms has Hamming weight <= 4.
Numbers with consecutive positive decimal digits after the digits are sorted.

Starting with a(1) = 1, a(n) = smallest nonnegative integer not yet in the sequence such that the first digit of a(n) is plus or minus one the last digit of a(n-1) plus or minus 1, with preference given +1 when possible. The digit 0 is not allowed.
Eternal domination number for P_3 X P_n grid graph.
In primorial base: a(n) is obtained by replacing each nonzero digit of n with its inverse (see Comments for precise definition).
Triangle T(n, k), n > 0 and 0 <= k < n, read by rows; if gcd(n, k) = 1, then T(n, k) = modular inverse of k (mod n), otherwise T(n, k) = k.

Starting from one digit move right by x steps, x being the value of the digit. If the steps go beyond the least significant digits they continue from the left side. Then repeat the process from the reached digit. The sequence lists the numbers such that all the digits are touched just one time and the last run ends in the initial digit.
Irregular triangular array T(m,k) with m (row) >= 1 and k (column) >= 1 read by rows: number of m-digit numbers whose digit sum is k.
Numbers that are not the product of two distinct composite numbers (A002808).
Number of 2-digit numbers whose digits add up to n.
a(n) = smallest integer not yet in the sequence with no digits shared with the previous term a(n-1), no repeated digits, and no 0-digit allowed.
n for which a Factor Pair Latin Square of order n exists.

Consider the digit reverse of a number x. Take the sum of these digits and repeat the process deleting the first addend and adding the previous sum. The sequence lists the numbers that after some iterations reach a sum equal to x.

Define two sequences n1(i) and n2(i) by the recurrences n1(i) = n1(i-1) + digsum(n2(i-1)), n2(i) = n2(i-1) + digsum(n1(i-1)), with initial values n1(1) = n and n2(1) = 0. Then a(n) is the smallest m such that n1(i) = n2(i) = m for some i, or -1 if no such m exists.
Record lengths of transient part of the unitary aliquot sequences of the numbers in A290143.
a(n) is the integer resulting from the concatenation of the unit digit of n-1 to the digits of n without its own unit digit.
Increasing sequence a(n)>a(n-1) where a(n)=smallest integer not yet in the sequence with no digits shared with the previous term a(n-1), no repeated digits, and no 0-digit allowed.
Increasing sequence where a(n) is the smallest integer not yet in the sequence with no digits shared with the term a(n-2), no repeated digits, and no 0-digit allowed.
Increasing sequence where a(n) is the smallest integer not yet in the sequence with no digits shared with the terms a(n-1) and a(n-2), no repeated digits, and no 0-digit allowed.
Maximal number of binary vectors of length n such that the unions (or bitwise ORs) of any 3 distinct vectors are all distinct.

Let F denote the two-way infinite sequence of Fibonacci numbers (for all positive or negative integers k, F(k+2)=F(k)+F(k+1) with F(0)=0, F(1)=1). Sequence lists positive numbers that are the difference between two terms of F.
Number of partitions of n into Pell parts (A000129).
Positive integers whose digits are in increasing order and whose successive digits differ by exactly 2.
Positive integers with digits in decreasing order that differ by 2.
Numbers in at least one Fibonacci sequence starting with two 1-digit numbers.
Lexicographically earliest such sequence a that a(i) = a(j) => A003557(i) = A003557(j) and A048250(i) = A048250(j), for all i, j.

Restricted growth sequence transform of A292268; filter combining multiplicative order of 2 mod 2n+1 and the number of trailing 1's in binary expansion of 2n+1.
List of numbers k whose consecutive digits increase or decrease by d-1, where d is the number of digits in k.

Irregular table where row n lists the positive integers k not divisible by 10 such that f(kN) = f(N) for N = A292683(n) and f(x) = x / (x without its first digit: A217657(x)).

Self-inverse permutation of natural numbers: replace (with multiplicity) each prime factor A000040(k) with A000040(min+(max-k)) in the prime factorization of n, where min = A055396(n) and max = A061395(n).
Triangular array read by rows: row n >= 1 is the list of integers from 0 to 2n-1.

Position of the prime ant after n steps. If the value of the ant's position is prime, it steps to the right; if the value is composite, it divides by the least divisor, steps to the left, and adds the divisor.
Numbers k such that A007755(k) is prime.
Numbers k such that c(k,0) < c(k,1), where c(k,d) = number of d's in the first k digits of the base-2 expansion of sqrt(2).
Number of ways to write A294357(n) as a sum of 3 odd primes p+q+r, with p>=q>=r.
Self-slideable numbers: numbers which can reproduce themselves by sliding each digit d by d places either to the left or to the right.
Demlo numbers: concat(L,M,R) where M and L + R are repdigits using the same digit, see comments for details.
Numbers k such that the positions of the ones in the binary representation of k are in arithmetic progression.
Lexicographically earliest sequence such that a(i) = a(j) => f(i) = f(j), where f(n) = [A003557(n), A046523(n), A048250(n)].
Self-inverse permutation of natural numbers: in prime factorization of n replace each positive prime exponent e with max + min - e, where max = A051903(n) and min = A051904(n).

Take the sequence of nonnegative integers whose decimal digits are not in strictly increasing order. Partition the sequence into subsequences whose elements are consecutive integers. Then a(n) is the number of elements in the n-th partition.

Lexicographically earliest sequence of distinct positive terms such that, for any n > 0, Sum_{k = 1..n} 10^(k-1) * a(k) can be computed without carry in decimal base.
Lexicographically earliest sequence of distinct positive terms such that, for any n> 0, Sum_{k = 1..n} 10^(n-k) * a(k) can be computed without carry in decimal base.
a(n) = smallest integer not yet in the sequence with no digits in common with a(n-1), a(n-2), and a(n-3); a(0)=0, a(1)=1, a(2)=2.
Square array T(n, k), n >= 0, k >= 0, read by antidiagonals upwards: T(n, k) = the (k+1)-th nonnegative number m such that n + m can be computed with carry in decimal base.
Matula-Goebel numbers of rooted trees such that every branch of the root has the same number of leaves.
Numbers k such that the digital sum of k and the digital root of k have the same parity.
Lexicographically earliest sequence of distinct positive terms such that, for any n > 1, if prime(k) is the least prime factor of a(n) then k divides a(n+1) (where prime(k) denotes the k-th prime).

Numbers without digit 1 whose multiplicative digital root is not 0.

Number of strict integer partitions of n in which the even parts appear as often at even positions as at odd positions.
Consider the concatenation of a(n) and a(n+1) as the integer A; consider the concatenation of the last digit of a(n) and the first digit of a(n+1) as the integer B. Now A is divisible by B.
Denominator of mean of first n primes.
Smallest distance from n to a prime power (as defined in A246547).
Distance from n to nearest Catalan number.

a(n) = distance from n to nearest Fibbinary number (A003714).

Permutation of natural numbers mapping ordinary factorization to "Ludic factorization": a(1) = 1, a(2n) = 2*a(n), a(A003961(n)) = A269379(a(n)).
Permutation of natural numbers mapping "Ludic factorization" to ordinary factorization: a(1) = 1, a(2n) = 2*a(n), a(A269379(n)) = A003961(a(n)).
Permutation of nonnegative integers: a(0) = 0; for n >= 1, a(n) = A057889(1+A057889(n-1)), where A057889 is a bijective bit-reverse.
Permutation of nonnegative integers: a(0) = 0; for n >= 1, a(n) = 1+A057889(A057889(n)-1), where A057889 is a bijective bit-reverse.
Numbers n with the property that for every m coprime to n, there are solutions to x^(psi(n)/ord(m,n)) == m (mod n), where psi(n) = A002322(n) and ord(m,n) is multiplicative order of m modulo n.
Lexicographically first sequence of distinct terms such that any set of three successive digits can be reordered as {d, d+1, d+2}, d being the smallest of the three digits.
Products of any power of 2 with prime numbers of prime-power index, i.e., prime numbers p of the form p = prime(q^k), for q prime, k >= 1.
Lexicographically first sequence of distinct terms such that any set of four successive digits can be reordered as {d, d+1, d+2, d+3}, d being the smallest of the four digits.
Lexicographically first sequence of distinct terms such that any set of five successive digits can be reordered as {d, d+1, d+2, d+3, d+4}, d being the smallest of the five digits.
Lexicographically first sequence of distinct terms such that any set of six successive digits can be reordered as {d, d+1, d+2, d+3, d+4, d+5}, d being the smallest of the six digits.

Numbers whose prime indices are powers of a common prime number.
Replacing each term of this sequence S with its digit-sum produces a new sequence S' such that S' and S share the same succession of digits.
Numbers k whose sum and product of digits are substrings of k.
Lexicographically earliest sequence of distinct positive terms such that, for any n > 0, A000120(a(n)) <= A053735(a(n+1)).
Replacing each term of this sequence S with the product of its digits produces a new sequence S' such that S' and S share the same succession of digits.
Group number of n-th element in the periodic table, or 0 if the element does not have a group number.
Lexicographically earliest sequence of distinct terms such that the successive quantities of digits between two successive 8's are given by the succession of the sequence's digits itself.
Lexicographically earliest sequence of distinct terms such that the successive quantities of digits between two successive 9's are given by the succession of the sequence's digits itself.
a(n) = n for n <= 11. Thereafter a(n) = a(n-a(n-2)) + a(n-a(n-4)) + a(n-a(n-6)).
7-smooth numbers representable as the sum of two relatively prime 7-smooth numbers.
Numbers equal to the determinant of a circulant matrix based on the base-9 digits of n.
Integers k such that the digits of k together with a single supplementary digit can be reordered to form a base-10 palindrome.
Amount by which n exceeds the largest binary palindrome less than or equal to n.
Numbers k such that abs(60*k^2 - 1710*k + 12150) +- 1 are twin primes.
Union of the prime powers (p^k, p prime, k >= 0) and numbers that are the product of 2 or more distinct primes.
A fractal-like sequence: erasing all pairs of consecutive terms that have at least one digit in common leaves the sequence unchanged.
A fractal-like sequence: erasing all pairs of consecutive terms a(n) and a(n+1) having the property that the last digit of a(n) is the same as the first digit of a(n+1) leaves the sequence unchanged.
Numbers that yield a prime when prime(k) is inserted after the k-th digit, for any k >= 1, k < number of digits.
Numbers that yield a prime when '2' is inserted between the first and second digit, or prime(k+1) is inserted after the k-th digit for any k > 1, k < number of digits.
Numbers that yield a prime whenever a '1' is inserted between any two digits.
Numbers which yield a prime whenever a '2' is inserted between any single pair of adjacent digits.
Numbers that yield a prime whenever a '3' is inserted between any two digits.

Numbers with weakly increasing prime multiplicities.

Solution (b(n)) of the complementary equation a(n) = b(2n) + b(3n) ; see Comments.

If pd(x) is the product of the digits of the number x and sd(x) the sum of the digits of the number x then the sequence lists all the positive numbers n for which pd(n) = sd(n) and sd(pd(n)) = pd(sd(n)).
In primorial base: a(n) is obtained by replacing each nonzero digit of n with its product with the nonzero digits at lower indices (See Comments for precise definition).

Take the sum of the digits of a number, put it at the left side and delete the same number of digits at the right side. Repeat the process. Sequence lists numbers that reach themselves after some steps.
Numbers n such that for every k = 1, 2, ..., A305706(n)-1, it is possible to insert plus signs into the decimal representation of n^k to make sum equal n.
Heinz numbers of reducible integer partitions. Numbers n > 1 that are prime or whose prime indices are relatively prime and such that A181819(n) is already in the sequence.

Filter sequence for all such sequences S, for which S(A091206(k)) = constant for all k >= 3, where A091206 gives primes whose binary representation encodes a polynomial irreducible over GF(2).
Irregular table: row n >= 0 lists all k >= 0 such that the decimal representation of 6^k has n digits '0' (conjectured).
Irregular table: row n >= 0 lists all k >= 0 such that the decimal representation of 2^k has n digits '0' (conjectured).

Matula-Goebel numbers of rooted semi-identity trees.

Numbers k with property that the arithmetic mean of any subset of its digits is an integer.
Square array A(n,k), n >= 1, k >= 0, read by antidiagonals: A(n,k) = Sum_{j=1..n} floor(n/j^k).

An irregular fractal sequence: underline all terms that share at least one digit with the preceding one. All underlined terms rebuild the starting sequence. (See the Comments section for more details.)
Least number k such that the determinant of the circulant matrix formed by its decimal digits is equal to n.
Positive integers equal to the permanent of the circulant matrix formed by their decimal digits.
Lexicographically earliest sequence of distinct positive terms such that the binary representation of the sum of two consecutive terms has at most 2 runs of ones.
Sprague-Grundy values for Maharaja Nim on the counterclockwise square spiral.
Numbers k such that every prime p <= sqrt(k) divides k*(k-1).
Numbers k such that the digits of k in base 10 are a permutation of those of k in some other base.
Let decimal expansion of n be d_1 d_2 ... d_k; a(n) = Sum_{i=1..k-1} Sum_{j=i+1..k} (d_i + d_j).
Numbers k with property that no two divisors of k share a common digit.
Numbers that are the sum of a prime number and a nonnegative cube.
a(n) is the determinant of the Vandermonde matrix of the digits of n.
a(n) is the square root of A034175(n) + A034175(n+1).
a(n) is the cubic root of A175428(n) + A175428(n+1).
Least number k such that the determinant of the symmetric Toeplitz matrix formed by its decimal digits is equal to n.
List of y-coordinates of successive points on the lower of the two lines formed by the terms of A308007.
Numbers k such that k is the substring identical to the most significant digits of its base-9 representation.
Least number k such that the determinant of the symmetric Hankel matrix formed by its decimal digits is equal to n.

Positive integers equal to the permanent of Hankel matrix formed by their decimal digits.

"Autotomy numbers" have two properties: (1) they have distinct decimal digits, and (2) subtracting their last digit from the remaining part produces another autotomy number (the numbers 1 to 9 are considered to be part of the sequence).
Lexicographically earliest sequence of distinct terms such that reading one-by-one the central digit of each term is the same as reading one-by-one the successive digits of the sequence itself.
Numbers that are divisible by the sum of the digits of the product of their digits.
Numbers k such that k in base 10 contains the same digits as k in some other base.
a(n) is the least nonnegative number whose digits do not appear in order (not necessarily consecutively) in the concatenation of all previous terms.
Numbers divisible by the LCM of all sums of any two digits (at distinct positions).
Numbers with no 0 digit that are divisible by the sum of any two of their digits at distinct positions.
a(n) is the least integer k such that both k^2+2*n-1 and k^2+4*n are squares.
Integers m such that A053319(m) is a term in A014574.
Numbers k such that -k is a quadratic nonresidue modulo all odd primes p <= sqrt(k) which do not divide k.
Langton's ant on a truncated hexagonal tiling: number of black cells after n moves of the ant when starting on a dodecagon and looking towards an edge where the dodecagon meets a triangle.
Langton's ant on a rhombitrihexagonal tiling: number of black cells after n moves of the ant when starting on a hexagon.
Number of black squares after n moves of a variant of Langton's ant with turns of 45 degrees.
Number subsets {0, ..., 10^k - 1} written in base 10 and sorted lexicographically, for k = 1, 2, ...
Inverse of A309589: 0-based positions in the number subsets {0, ..., 10^k - 1} written in base 10 and sorted lexicographically, for k = 1, 2, ...
Number of even parts appearing among the second largest parts of the partitions of n into 3 parts.
Product of digits of (n written in base 9).
Numbers k such that A274016(k) = k - 1.
Numbers, with digits in nondecreasing order, whose product of digits equals the number of digits times the sum of digits.

Matula-Goebel numbers of rooted trees where all terminal rooted subtrees are either constant or strict.
Heinz numbers of totally strong integer partitions.
Numbers k such that A000009(k) divides k!.
Numbers whose prime multiplicities are pairwise indivisible.
Numbers k such that the smallest digit of k is equal to the additive digital root of k (in base 10).
Heinz numbers of alternately co-strong integer partitions.
Numbers with a noncomposite number of 1's in their binary expansion.
Heinz numbers of fully normal integer partitions.
Heinz numbers of uniformly normal integer partitions.
Uniform tree numbers. Matula-Goebel numbers of uniform rooted trees.
Uniform relatively prime tree numbers. Matula-Goebel numbers of uniform relatively prime rooted trees.
Let b(1) = b(2) = 1; for n >= 3, b(n) = b(t(n)) + b(n-t(n)) where t = A287422. a(n) = 2*b(n) - n.
Let b(1) = b(2) = 1; for n >= 3, b(n) = n - b(t(n)) - b(n-t(n)) where t = A004001. a(n) = 2*b(n) - n.
Filter sequence constructed from the coefficients of the Stern polynomials B(d,t) collected for each divisor d of n. Restricted growth sequence transform of A317944.
Numbers with digits in nondecreasing order such that additive and multiplicative digital roots coincide.
Numbers with digits in nondecreasing order and with multiplicative digital root > 0.
Numbers with digits in nondecreasing order without digit 1 whose multiplicative digital root is not 0.
a(n) is the denominator of Sum_{d|n} Sum_{j|d} 1/j.
Integers a(n) such that [a(n) - k] is a palindrome in base 10, with k <10.
Integers a(n) such that [a(n) + k] is a palindrome in base 10, with k < 10.
Absolute value of negative records in A318734.
Filter sequence combining the prime signature of n (A046523) with the prime signature of its conjugated prime factorization (A278221).
Filter sequence combining the prime signature of n (A046523) with the largest prime factor of n (A006530).
Filter sequence combining the prime signature of n (A046523) with A289625.

Lexicographically earliest infinite sequence such that a(i) = a(j) => A000010(i) = A000010(j) and A046523(i) = A046523(j), for all i, j >= 1, where A046523(n) is the smallest number with same prime signature as n, and A000010 is the Euler totient function.
Numbers whose consecutive prime indices are divisible. Heinz numbers of integer partitions in which each part is divisible by the next.
The y coordinates of the shell enumeration of N X N where N = {0, 1, 2, ...}(A319514).
Filter sequence combining the prime signature of phi(d) from all divisors d > 1 of n.

The x coordinates of the stripe enumeration of N X N where N = {0, 1, 2, ...}.
The y coordinates of the stripe enumeration of N X N where N = {0, 1, 2, ...}.

Filter sequence which records for primes their residue modulo 6, and for all other numbers assigns a unique number.

Heinz numbers of spanning sum-product knapsack partitions.

Filter sequence for counting the residue classes mod 6 of divisors of n.

Numbers not of the form [p^c] + [q^c] + [r^c] + [s^c] + [t^c] where p, q, r, s, and t are prime, c = 41/20 = 2.05, and [...] is the floor function.
Number of weakly unimodal compositions of n in which the greatest part occurs exactly eight times.
Number of weakly unimodal compositions of n in which the greatest part occurs exactly nine times.
Number of weakly unimodal compositions of n in which the greatest part occurs exactly ten times.
Keep just the digits of n that appear exactly once; write -1 if all digits disappear.
Keep just the digits of n that appear exactly once; write 0 if all digits disappear.
Possible total numbers of pips when rolling two dice in backgammon.
a(n) is the product of n and all its decimal digits individually except the leftmost digit.
Smallest positive number for which the 4th power cannot be written as sum of 4th powers of any subset of previous terms.

n such that all n - s are squarefree numbers where s is a squarefree number in range n/2 <= s < n.
Reverse the nonzero digits of n.
Reverse runs of nonzero digits in ternary expansion of n and convert back to decimal.
Delete all consecutive identical decimal digits of n; write 0 if all digits disappear.
Delete all consecutive identical decimal digits of n; write -1 if all digits disappear.
Positive numbers for which the product of digits is equal to the power tower of digits (right-associative).

Sum of digits of n minus the number of digits of n.
Digits of n interpreted in factorial base: a(Sum d_k*10^k) = Sum d_k*k!
Lexicographically earliest such sequence a that a(i) = a(j) => A046523(i) = A046523(j) and A048250(i) = A048250(j), for all i, j.
a(n) = number of occurrences of the decimal representation of n in the concatenation of all terms preceding a(n), or n if there are no such occurrences.

The number of digits used in the sequence up to a(n) [a(n) included] is a multiple of a(n). The sequence starts with a(1) = 1 and is always extended with the smallest integer not yet present in the sequence that does not lead to a contradiction.
Reverse runs of zeros in binary expansion of n and convert back to decimal.
Reverse runs of ones in binary expansion of n and convert back to decimal.
Nonnegative numbers whose digits can be formed by typing adjacent keys on a 123-456-789 keypad without repeating a digit and without changing direction.
a(n) is the minimal absolute difference between n and each of the powers of the previous terms; a(1) = 1.

Langton's ant on a tiling with vertex types (3.12.12; 3.4.3.12): number of black cells after n moves of the ant when starting on a dodecagon and looking towards an edge where it meets another dodecagon.

For a nonnegative number m with decimal digits (d_1, ..., d_k), let s(m) be the area of the convex hull of the set of points { (i, d_i), i = 1..k }; a(n) = 2 * s(n).

Sums of no more than two 5-smooth numbers.

A variant of the Syracuse-like routine visible in A323175, avoiding duplicates (and loops). See the Comments section.

Lexicographically earliest sequence such that a(i) = a(j) => A000035(i) = A000035(j) and A003557(i) = A003557(j) and A048250(i) = A048250(j), for all i, j.

Lexicographically earliest sequence of terms describing its successive chunks of different digits.
a(n) is the multiplicity of the rarest values appearing recorded in n-th pair in A324078.
Numbers n such that A324108(n) = A324054(n-1).
Number of zerofree nonnegative integers <= n.
Lexicographically earliest sequence of different terms starting with a(1) = 2 such that the n-th digit of the sequence, placed in front of a(n) and then concatenated, produces a composite number.

Decimal expansion of a normal number in base 10, which, on average, up to any given integer appearance (above 11), is more compact than Champernowne's constant, and more compact than A189823.

Lexicographically earliest sequence of distinct terms such that a(n) is not divisible by any digit of a(n+1).

a(1) = 1. Thereafter, if n is prime, a(n) is the next prime after a(n-1), but written backwards. If n is not prime, a(n) is the next composite after a(n-1), written backwards.
a(n) is the sum of each distinct digit in n, raised to the power of its number of appearances in n.
a(n) = (sum of digits of n) mod (sum of digits of n+1).
BII-numbers of set-systems that are closed under nonempty intersection.
For any n >= 0: consider the different ways to split the binary representation of n into two (possibly empty) parts, say with value x and y; a(n) is the least possible value of x + y.
For any n >= 0: consider the different ways to split the binary representation of n into two (possibly empty) parts, say with value x and y; a(n) is the least possible value of max(x, y).

The first repeating term in the trajectory of n under iterations of A329623, or -1 if no such terms exists.
Numbers whose lengths of runs of 1's in their reversed binary expansion are weakly increasing.
a(n) is the number of entries from a(0) to a(n-2) that have the same number of digits as a(n-1), with a(0) = 0.
Numbers whose prime signature is a necklace.
The ghost iteration (A): add or subtract the number formed by absolute differences of digits (A040115), according to parity (even or odd).
The ghost iteration (B): add or subtract the number formed by absolute differences of digits (A040115), according to parity (odd or even).
a(0)=0. If a(n)=k is the first occurrence of k then a(n+1)=a(k), otherwise a(n+1)=n-m where m is the index of the greatest prior term.
Smallest palindrome k, not less than n, such that k is also a palindrome in base n.
Numbers whose digits are in nondecreasing order in bases 9 and 10.
If the run lengths in binary expansion of n are (r(1), ..., r(w)), then the run lengths in binary expansion of a(n) are (r(1), r(3), r(5), ..., r(6), r(4), r(2)).
Numbers which are not the sum of two squarefree semiprimes.
The absolute value of the difference between n and A053392(n), the concatenation of the sums of every pair of consecutive digits of n.
Numbers that are either odd or are congruent to {+-4, +-6, +-8, +-10} (mod 32).
a(n) is the smallest positive k such that box(k,n) is a positive square, where box(k,n) is Eric Angelini's mapping defined in the Comments.
Integers k such that the length of decimal expansion of k^k is a repdigit.
MM-numbers of achiral multisets of multisets.
MM-numbers of fully chiral multisets of multisets.
Lexicographically earliest sequence of nonnegative terms such that for any n > 0 and k > 0, a(n+2*k) <> max(a(n), a(n+k)).
a(n) is the least nonnegative integer k such that n XOR k is a square (where XOR denotes the bitwise XOR operator).
a(n) is the least nonnegative integer k such that n XOR k is a cube (where XOR denotes the bitwise XOR operator).
Number of times A329985(n) has appeared in A329985 (including the present occurrence).
Table of strictly decreasing sequences with terms in {0, ..., 9}, sorted by length, then lexicographically.

Consider integers k=0,1,2,... as strings. Compare each digit in the string, in left-to-right order, with the contents of a bag (multiset) of digits, which is initially empty. If digit d is in the bag delete d from both the string and the bag. What remains of any nonempty string is appended to the sequence and its digits are added to the bag.
The concatenation of the products of every pair of consecutive digits of n (with a(n) = 0 for 0 <= n <= 9).
Numbers k such that every vertex-transitive graph of order k is a Cayley-graph.
Numbers k that are divisible by all integers less than or equal to the cube root of k.
a(n) is n transformed by the "successive Oware operation" (see the Comments and Example sections).
Numbers k such that both k and k + 1 are Niven numbers.
Numbers that cannot be written as the sum of four proper powers. A proper power is an integer of the form a^b where a,b are integers greater than or equal to 2.

For any n >= 0: consider all pairs of numbers (x, y) whose binary representations can be interleaved (or shuffled) to produce the binary representation of n (possibly with leading zeros); a(n) is the least possible value of x + y.
Numbers k such that for any decimal digit d in k, the remainder when k is divided by d+1 is d.
For any number n >= 0 with decimal digits (d_1, d_2, ..., d_k), the decimal expansion of a(n) is (n mod (1+d_1), n mod (1+d_2), ..., n mod (1+d_k)).
Remeven numbers: having an even remainder modulo any of their digits, digit 0 forbidden.
Lexicographically earliest sequence of distinct positive terms such that for any n > 0, the n-th term and the n-th digit have the same parity.
Values k for successive maximal records of the function A defined as A(prime(k)) = log(prime(k)) - prime(k)/Pi(prime(k)) where Pi(prime(k)) is number of primes <= prime(k).
Lexicographically earliest sequence of distinct positive numbers such that for any n > 0, the n-th nonzero decimal digit in the sequence divides the n-th term.
Numbers k such that there is no prime p between k and (9/8)k, exclusive.
a(n) is the number of digits in the concatenation of a(0) to a(n-1) that are equal to the corresponding digit in the concatenation of all integers >= 0, with a(0) = 0.
a(n) = min(n, A057889(n)), where A057889 is bijective base-2 reverse.
a(n) = min(n, A289234(n)), where A289234 is primorial base "reciprocal" flip.
Numbers k such that k/(digsum(k)) is an integer cube.
Lexicographically earliest sequence of distinct positive integers such that four successive digits are always distinct.
a(n) is the least divisor u of A331221(n) such that the decimal representations of u and of A331221(n)/u have the same number of digits d for d = 0..9.
a(n) is the greatest divisor v of A331221(n) such that the decimal representations of v and of A331221(n)/v have the same number of digits d for d = 0..9.
Lexicographically earliest infinite sequence such that a(i) = a(j) => A001222(i) = A001222(j) and A061395(i) = A061395(j) for all i, j.
Lexicographically earliest infinite sequence such that a(i) = a(j) => f(i) = f(j), where f(n) = min(n, A057889(n)), and A057889 is a bijective base-2 reverse.
a(n) is the number of times the digit 1 appears in the concatenation of integers from 0 to n, minus the number of times the next most frequent digit appears.
The grid points visible from the central point of an infinite 2D square lattice where all grid points are numbered as in the Ulam spiral.
Consider the different ways to split the decimal representation of n into palindromic parts; a(n) is the greatest possible sum of the parts of such a split.
Lexicographically earliest sequence of distinct positive terms such that a(n), a(n+1) and a(n) + a(n+1) have no digit in common.
One and all numbers whose prime indices are pairwise coprime and already belong to the sequence, where a singleton is always considered to be coprime.
Lexicographically earliest infinite sequence such that a(i) = a(j) => A009194(i) = A009194(j) and A331166(i) = A331166(j) for all i, j.
Lexicographically earliest sequence of distinct positive integers such that (last digit of a(n)) < (first digit of a(n+1)).
Numbers with at most one prime prime index, counted with multiplicity.
Lexicographically earliest sequence of distinct positive integers such that three successive digits are always distinct.
Lexicographically earliest sequence of distinct positive integers such that five successive digits are always distinct.
Numbers with at most one distinct prime prime index.
Numbers that are not the sum of nine (9) positive cubes.
Numbers that are not the sum of ten (10) positive cubes.
Numbers that are not the sum of eleven (11) positive cubes.
Nonnegative numbers ordered by number of digits, and then by sum of digits, and then by value.
Numbers that yield a prime whenever a '4' is inserted between any two digits.

Positive integers r such that B(1,r) = B(2,r - 1) = ... = B(r,1) = 0, where B denotes the function mapping every pair of positive integers (m,n) into 1 if m * 2^(n + 2) + 1 is a prime number dividing F(n), where F(n) denotes the n-th Fermat number (i.e., F(n) = A000215(n)); and into 0 otherwise.
Even bisection of A332662: the x-coordinates of an enumeration of N X N.
Numbers whose binary representation does not contain a square-subword of length 4 or more.
Positions of adjacent unequal terms in the sequence of differences between primes.
Numbers k such that every distinct consecutive subsequence of the k-th composition in standard order has a different sum.
a(1) = 0. For n>1, a(n+1) = the minimum positive m such that the concatenation of the decimal values [a(n-m),a(n-m+1),...,a(n-m+k)] equals a(n) for some k>=0; a(n+1) = a(n) + 1 if no such m exists.
First index of partially unequal prime quartets.

The contamination sequence: a digit d must be separated from any other digit d by at least d digits different from d; this is the lexicographically earliest infinite sequence of distinct integers with this property.
Numbers m such that m! has a palindromic number of decimal digits.
a(n) is the greatest number m not yet in the sequence such that the decimal expansions of n and of m have the same digits (up to order but with multiplicity).
Smallest k > 0 with gcd(k, rev(k)) = n, where rev(k) is digit reversal of k and with sum of digits of k = n, or 0 if no such k exists.
Scan the binary representation of n from left to right; at each 1, reverse the bits to the left and including this 1. The resulting binary representation is that of a(n).
a(n) is the digit sum of the concatenation of the decimal digits of n,n+1,...,n+k, where k >= 0 and minimal, such that the concatenation is divisible by its digit sum, or -1 if no such sum is known.
Lexicographically earliest array of distinct positive integers read row by row; a single row consists of integers using together exactly 10 distinct digits.
a(n) is the greatest integer q <= n such that for some r >= q, phi(q) + phi(r) = 2*n.
Irregular triangle read by rows: row n gives the members of the smallest nonnegative reduced residue system in the modified congruence modulo n by Brändli and Beyne, called mod* n.
a(n) is the least integer m >= 3 such that n is m-gonal pyramidal number.
a(n) is the least k such that the decimal representation of n appears as a substring in the concatenation of 0, 1, ..., k.
Numbers that are equal to the LCM of their palindromic divisors.
Numbers that can be written as a product of distinct palindromes.
Numbers k such that 70*k^2 + 70*k - 1 is prime.

The difference version of the 'Decade transform' : to obtain a(n) write n as a sum of its power-of-ten parts and then continue to calculate the absolute value of the difference between the adjacent parts until a single number remains.
Numbers m such that (m / sum of digits of m) is a palindrome.
Irregular triangle read by rows: row n gives the members of the smallest nonnegative reduced residue system in the modified congruence modulo 2*n - 1 by Brändli and Beyne, called mod*(2*n - 1).
The n-cowboy shootout problem: a(3^k) = 3^k, a((3^k)+b) = b if (3^k)+b <= 2*3^k, otherwise a((3^k)+b) = 2*b-3^k, where b is a positive integer.
Numbers m such that m^2 = p^2 + k^2, with p > 0, where p = A007954(m) = the product of digits of m.
Positive integers m such that sum of cubes of the digits of m, t=A055012(m), is a multiple of m (m/A055012(m) is an integer >= 1).
a(n) is the least number that can be reached starting from n and iterating the nondeterministic map x -> x/d where d is a proper divisor of x whose decimal representation appears in that of x.
Numbers that divide the multiplication of its digits raised to their own powers.
Numbers whose XOR-triangles have reflection symmetry.
Positive integers k such that there exists a positive integer m consisting of k identical digits and such that m is a multiple of k.
Numbers k such that the k-th composition in standard order (row k of A066099) has weakly decreasing non-adjacent parts.
Numbers k such that every subsequence (not necessarily contiguous) of the k-th composition in standard order (A066099) has a different sum.
Heinz numbers of alternately strong integer partitions.
Numbers whose binary representation encodes a (binary) max-heap on elements from the set {0,1} with root at the most significant bit.
Binary interpretation of the left diagonal of the EQ-triangle with first row generated from the binary expansion of n, with most significant bit given by first row.
Numbers m equal to |d_1^k + Sum_{j=2..k} (-1)^j*d_j^k| where d_1 d_2 ... d_k is the decimal expansion of m.
Numbers of m digits which are equal to the absolute value of the sum of the m-th powers of their digits, with alternating signs.
Numbers k such that the k-th composition in standard order (A066099) is pairwise coprime, where a singleton is always considered coprime.
Lexicographically earliest sequence of distinct positive terms whose Recamán transform has only distinct values.
Lexicographically earliest strictly increasing sequence of positive integers whose Recamán transform has only distinct values.
Heinz numbers of totally co-strong integer partitions.
Numbers k such that the k-th composition in standard order (A066099) avoids the pattern (1,2,1).
Numbers k such that the k-th composition in standard order (A066099) avoids the pattern (2,1,2).
The successive absolute differences between two digits are the successive absolute differences between two terms.
The successive absolute differences between two digits are the successive differences between two terms. See in the Comments section why a(n) = a(n-1) sometimes.
Numbers k such that the k-th composition in standard order (A066099) avoids the pattern (1,1,2).
Numbers k such that the k-th composition in standard order (A066099) avoids the pattern (2,1,1).
Numbers k such that the k-th composition in standard order (A066099) avoids the pattern (2,2,1).
Numbers k such that the k-th composition in standard order (A066099) avoids the pattern (1,2,2).

Squares visited by a fairy chess wazir moving on a square-spiral numbered board where the wazir moves to the unvisited square containing the spiral number with the fewest divisors. In case of a tie it chooses the square with the lowest spiral number.
Number of partitions of n into exactly two parts with no decimal carries.
a(n) is the player who has highest winning probability in the "Random Josephus Game" with n players.
Sigma(k) has at least the same number of distinct prime factors as k.
Square array read by descending antidiagonals T(n,k): In the binary expansion of n, reverse the order of the bits in the same position as the active bits in A057716(k).
Numbers k such that for 1 <= i < j <= h, all sigma(p_i^e_i), sigma(p_j^e_j) are pairwise coprime, when k = p_1^e_1 * ... * p_h^e_h, where each p_i^e_i is the maximal power of prime p_i dividing k.
Numbers k such that A336456(n) = Product_{p^e|n} A336456(p^e). Here each p^e is the maximal power of prime p that divides k, and A336456(n) = A335915(sigma(sigma(n))).
Numbers with decimal expansion d_1, ..., d_w such that d_k = d*_{k + d_k} for k = 1..w where d* is the w-periodic sequence with initial terms d_1, ..., d_w.
Irregular triangle in which row n lists residues k found in the sequence Lucas(i) mod n.
a(n) = 1 + the total remainder when repeatedly taking integer square roots until 1 is reached.

For any number n whose set of nonzero decimal digits is { d_0, ..., d_k } (with d_0 < ... < d_k), a(n) is obtained by replacing in the decimal representation of n each nonzero digit d_m by d_{k-m} for m = 0..k.
Numbers that cannot be written as the sum of 5 or less squares of composite numbers, allowing repetitions (complement of A055075).
Positive integers k such that the number of steps it takes to reach 1 in the '3x+1' problem is different for all j < k.
Numbers divisible by their first digit and their last digit.
Numbers that are a divisor of the product of the digits of its divisors.
a(n) is the greatest number m not yet in the sequence such that the binary expansions of n and of m have the same runs of consecutive equal digits (up to order but with multiplicity).
a(n) is the length of the largest run of contiguous grid points on the n-th antidiagonal of the Even Conant lattice that are not on an edge, or 0 if no such point exists.
Numbers all of whose divisors are Niven numbers (A005349).
Smallest integer m such that the sum of the first m prime numbers is greater than n^2.
a(n) is n + the number of digits in the decimal expansion of n.
a(n) is the number formed by removing from n each digit if it is a duplicate of the previous digit, from left to right.
Digits of n rearranged to be the smallest number with the fewest possible prime factors, counted with multiplicity. Terms retain the same number of digits as n, i.e. leading digits may not be zero.
Irregular triangle read by rows: T(n, k) gives the primitive period of the sequence {k (Modd n)}_{k >= 0}, for n >= 1.
Numbers whose divisors are all Zuckerman numbers (A007602).
Integers m such that A337454(m) = tau(m), the number of divisors of n.
Positive integers k with digits in nondecreasing order for which the digital sum contains the same distinct digits as the digital product.
If a(n) has at least one common digit with a(n-1), underline a(n). The non-underlined terms reproduce the sequence itself.
Numbers whose set of distinct prime indices (A304038) is pairwise coprime, where a singleton is always considered coprime.
Floor of (digital root of n) divided by (number of digits in n).
Least number of heptagonal pyramidal numbers needed to represent n.
a(0) = 0; for n > 0, a(n) is the least positive integer not occurring earlier such that the digits in a(n-1)*a(n) are all distinct.
Numbers k such that 398*k^2 - 1 is prime.
Least number of octagonal numbers needed to represent n.
Least number of centered heptagonal numbers needed to represent n.
Least number of pentagonal pyramidal numbers needed to represent n.
Least number of hexagonal pyramidal numbers needed to represent n.
Least number of octagonal pyramidal numbers needed to represent n.
Least number of odd cubes needed to represent n.
Numbers that are either a power of a prime or have relatively prime prime indices.
The largest e-squarefree e-divisor of n.
a(n) is the greatest number not yet in the sequence with the same number of digits and the same sum of digits as n.
a(n) is the greatest number not yet in the sequence with the same number of digits and the same largest digit as n.
a(n) is the greatest number not yet in the sequence with the same number of digits and the same smallest digit as n.
No even digit is present in a(n) + a(n+1).
Product of the nonzero digits of (n written in base 9).
Orders of elements of the Rubik's Cube group.
Possible number of digits in a factorial.
Lexicographically earliest sequence of distinct nonnegative terms such that the numbers of digits between successive 1s are distinct.
Number of (unordered) ways of making change for n US Dollars using the current US denominations of $1, $2, $5, $10, $20, $50 and $100 bills.
Seeds not producing -1 under the A339091 protocol. The complement of A339093.
a(n) = n + sod(n, sod(n, 10)), where sod(n,b) is the sum of base-b digits of n.
Pick any digit d; there are exactly d digits between d and the closest duplicate of d (either before or after) in the sequence.

Irregular triangle T(n, k), n, k >= 0, read by rows; for any number m with runs in binary expansion (r_1, ..., r_j), let R(m) = {r_1 + ... + r_j, r_2 + ... + r_j, ..., r_j}; row n corresponds to the numbers k such that R(k) is included in R(n), in ascending order.
Numbers k for which k-1 is a multiple of A053575(k) [the odd part of phi(k)].
Products of distinct primes or semiprimes.
n with the rightmost occurrence of the smallest digit of n deleted.

Lexicographically earliest sequence of distinct nonnegative terms such that for any n >= 0, a(n+1) is obtained by altering the leftmost decimal digit (which is not a leading zero) in a(n) or if this is not possible by altering the rightmost leading zero in a(n).
T(n, k) = Sum_{j=1..k} [n mod j <> 1], where [] is the Iverson bracket. Table read by rows.
T(n, k) is the number of integers that are less than or equal to k that do not divide n. Triangle read by rows, for 0 <= k <= n.
a(n) = (n')^A054054(n), where n' is the number resulting from removing the rightmost occurrence of the smallest digit of n, A054054(n).
a(n) = Sum_{d|n, d odd, d <= n/d} binomial(n/d, d).
Lexicographically earliest infinite sequence such that a(i) = a(j) => f(i) = f(j), where f(n) = [A291759(n), A278222(A304759(n))], for all i, j >= 1.
a(n) is the least k such that the digit reversal of k is greater than or equal to n.
List of X-coordinates of point moving along one of the arms of a counterclockwise square spiral with four arms; A340945 gives Y-coordinates.
a(n) is the smallest positive number m not yet in the sequence with the property that the sum of the even digits of m and the sum of the odd digits of m differ by n.
Fully multiplicative: for any prime p, if the reversal of p in base 10, say q, is prime, then a(p) = q, otherwise a(p) = p.
The sum of the prime digits of m and the sum of the nonprime digits of m differ by n.
Number of ways to write n as an ordered sum of 2 nonzero decimal palindromes.

Triangle read by columns T(n,k) k > n >= 1: Last survivor positions in a modified Josephus problem for n numbers, where after each deletion the counting starts over at the lowest existing number n, rather than continuing from the current position.
a(n) is the number of digits from the end of the concatenation of all previous terms where n last appears. If n has not previously appeared then a(n) = n.
Write n as a sum of powers of 2 then replace each power of 2 in the sum by its decimal reversal A004094(n).
Numbers k such that gcd(k, phi(k)) > log(log(k)).
Numbers k such that gcd(k, sigma(k)) > log(log(k)).
a(0) = 0; for n > 0, a(n) is the smallest positive integer not yet in the sequence such that the first digit of a(n) differs by 1 from the last digit of a(n-1).
a(0) = 0; for n > 0, a(n) is the smallest positive integer not yet in the sequence that can be created by adding 1 or -1, for digits > 0, to every digit in a(n-1).
a(0) = 0; for n > 0, a(n) is the smallest positive integer not yet in the sequence that can be created by adding 1, 0, or -1, for digits > 0, to every digit in a(n-1).
When a digit d in the digit-stream of this sequence is even, the next digit is > d.
When a digit d is odd, the next digit is > d.
When a digit d is prime, the next digit is > d.
Numbers for which the sum of digits equals the product of nonzero digits.
Numbers without an inferior odd divisor > 1.
Base-10 numbers m such that k*m = d||d||...||d (here || appears k-1 times), where k is the length of m, d is any m's digit and || represents concatenation.

A self-describing sequence: start with 0, then for each digit in each successive term, starting from the first term, append to the sequence its most recent position in the string formed by the concatenation of all previous terms.
Numbers with no adjacent prime indices having quotient < 1/2.
Numbers k with digits in nondecreasing order and satisfying k < (product of digits of k) * (sum of digits of k).
Numbers k such that gcd(k, Phi_k(a)) > 1 for some a, where Phi_k is the k-th cyclotomic polynomial.
Numbers divisible both by the product of their nonzero digits (A055471) and by the sum of their digits (A005349).
Lexicographically earliest sequence of distinct nonnegative terms such that both a(n) and a(n) + a(n+1) have digits in nondecreasing order.
k-digit positive numbers exactly one of whose substrings is divisible by k.
Heinz numbers of the integer partitions counted by A342337, which have all adjacent parts (x, y) satisfying either x = y or x = 2y.
a(0) = 0; for n > 0, a(n) is the least positive integer not occurring earlier such that both the digits in a(n) and the digits in a(n-1)*a(n) are all distinct.
a(1) = 1; for n > 1, a(n) is the least positive integer not occurring earlier such that a(n-1)+a(n) shares no digit with either a(n-1) or a(n).
a(1) = 2; for n > 1, a(n) is the least positive integer not occurring earlier such that a(n-1)*a(n) shares no digit with either a(n-1) or a(n).
Number k > 1 such that gpf(phi(k)/lambda(k)) = A006530(A000010(k)/A002322(k)) > log(log(k))^2.
Number of strict integer partitions of n with strictly increasing first quotients.
Heinz numbers of integer partitions with constant (equal) first quotients.
Heinz numbers of integer partitions with weakly increasing first quotients.
Heinz numbers of integer partitions with weakly decreasing first quotients.
Numbers k such that A340740(k) <= k.
Numbers divisible both by their nonzero individual digits and by the sum of their digits.
a(1) = 2; for n > 1, a(n) is the least positive integer not occurring earlier such that a(n) shares no digit with a(n-1) and a(n-1)*a(n) shares no digit with either a(n-1) or a(n).
Numbers k that divide the smallest number whose sum of digits is k.
Numbers k such that d(1)^0 + d(2)^1 + ... + d(p)^(p-1) = d(1)^(p-1) + d(2)^(p-2) + ... + d(p)^0, where d(i), i=1..p, are the digits of k.
a(n) is the smallest number whose sum of digits is equal to the sum of digits of n.
Remove duplicates in the decimal digit-reversal of n.
Distance to nearest product of 3 consecutive numbers (three-dimensional promic number, A007531).
7-smooth numbers not divisible by 10: positive numbers whose prime divisors are all <= 7 but do not contain both 2 and 5.
a(n) is the least term in A007602 that is divisible by A342950(n).
a(n) is the least term in A007602 such that the product of digits equals A342950(n) or 0 if no such number exists.
Zeroless numbers k ordered according to k/A007954(k), and in case of ties by k, where A007954(k) is the product of digits of k.
Positions of Zuckerman numbers within A342978, the ordered list of zeroless numbers according to k/A007954(k).
Zuckerman numbers (A007602) ordered by increasing value of k/A007954(k) where A007954(k) is the product of the decimal digits of k.
Numbers having exactly 1 divisor of the form 8*k + 1, that is, numbers with no divisor of the form 8*k + 1 other than 1.

For m >= 1, the m-digit number k = d_m||...||d_2||d_1 is a term if it is divisible by f_m(k) that is the sum of the m elementary symmetric polynomials in m variables e_i(k): f_m(k) = Sum_{i=1..m} e_i(d_1, ..., d_m).
a(n) is the product of the decimal digits of A343403(n).
Numbers k such that 2*k is a multiple of A045917(k).
Numbers that are not the sum of exactly four terms from A020330 (not necessarily distinct).
Numbers k such that the product of the digits of k is not the product of digits of any earlier term in the sequence.
Palindromes with digits strictly increasing up to the middle digit.
Niven (or Harshad) numbers which when divided by sum of their digits, give a quotient which is a Zuckerman number.
Zuckerman numbers which when divided by product of their digits, give a quotient which is also a Zuckerman number.
Zuckerman numbers which when divided by the product of their digits, give a quotient which is a Niven (Harshad) number.
Table read by rows: row n lists the residues of the triangular numbers modulo n.
Zuckerman numbers which divided by the product of their digits give integers which are also divisible by the product of their digits, and so on, until result is 1.

Let S be the set of all numbers that can be obtained by permuting the digits of n (leading zeros can be omitted). Then a(n) is that element of S with the smallest number of divisors. In case of a tie, choose the smallest.
Numbers k such that the alternating group A_k is not a Hurwitz group.
Numbers with decimal expansion (d_1, ..., d_k) such that all the sums d_i + ... + d_j with 1 <= i <= j <= k are distinct.

Numbers with binary expansion (b_1, ..., b_m) such that bending a strip of paper of length k+1 with an angle of +90 degrees (resp. -90 degrees) at position X=k when b_k = 1 (resp. b_k = 0) for k = 1..m yields a configuration where all edges are distinct.

Squares visited on a spirally numbered board when stepping to the closest unvisited square which contains a number that shares no digit with the number of the current square. If two or more such squares are the same distance away the one with the smaller number is chosen.
Lexicographically earliest sequence S of distinct nonnegative terms such that the n-th odd digit of S is present in the n-th odd term of S.
a(n) is the least k such that the sum of digits of k is a substring of n and the sum of digits of n is a substring of k.
a(n) is the least k such that n is divisible by the sum of digits of k and k is divisible by the sum of digits of n; a(n) = -1 if no such k exists.
Lexicographically earliest sequence S of distinct positive terms such that the product of the last k digits of S is even, k being the rightmost digit of a(n).
Numbers m with decimal expansion (d_k, ..., d_1) such that d_i = m * i mod 10 for i = 1..k.
Numbers m with decimal expansion (d_k, ..., d_1) such that d_i = m ^ i mod 10 for i = 1..k.
Numbers m with decimal expansion (d_1, ..., d_k) such that d_i = m * i mod 10 for i = 1..k.

4149: Walk along the hexagonal spiral, with its cells numbered starting at 0. Begin with no knights. If the square you are at is not attacked by an existing knight, place a knight there, otherwise leave it empty. The sequence lists the squares occupied by the knights.
4150: Primes such that all digits (except perhaps the least significant digit) are even.

An extension of the Jacobsthal numbers: 0, 0, 1, followed by A001045.

4156: a(x) = if one of {4x^2 - 146x + 1373, 4x^2 - 144x + 1459, 4x^2 - 142x + 1301, 4x^2 - 140x + 1877} is prime, then pick that prime in sequence.

Numbers of orders of nontrivial positive magic-squares with magic sum n. A nontrivial positive magic square is a k-by-k array of consecutive positive integers (not necessarily including 1) such that all rows, all columns and the two diagonals each add up to the same constant (the "magic sum"), with the additional restriction that k (the "order") is greater than 1.

Array T(n,k) read by antidiagonals, n,k >= 1: Start with a point at the origin of the n-dimensional grid. At each iteration, add a new point by increasing one of the coordinates of the current point by 1, choosing the option that gives the least maximum number of points on a line through the new point. In case of ties, compare the number of points on the line with the next largest number of points, etc. If there is still a tie, choose the first among the optimal coordinates. T(n,k) is the zero-based index of the coordinate that is increased in the k-th step.
